projects.title: Adjustable Bench Power Supply
projects.description: An adjustable bench supply designed for 2.5–38 V output and up to 20 A, with ESP32 monitoring, active cooling, and a 3D-printed enclosure.

caseStudy.statement: A configurable bench supply for testing circuits at different voltages and current limits.
caseStudy.problem: Bench testing needs adjustable power and visible output readings without the cost of a commercial lab supply.
caseStudy.built: The documented design combines a CC/CV buck converter, an ESP32, an INA228 power monitor, a TFT display, and temperature sensors. A custom enclosure houses the wiring, banana terminals, cooling fans, and circuit breaker.
caseStudy.difficulty: The README specifies voltage and current limits separately; achievable output depends on the operating point and upstream power supply.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository provides enclosure CAD, wiring diagrams, and a bill of materials. Its 500 W description, 600 W converter rating, and 480 W input supply do not establish a measured continuous output rating.

images.alt: CAD render of the adjustable power-supply enclosure

projects.title: Pico+ Devboard
projects.description: A compact custom RP2040 board with 16 MB flash, USB-C, battery input, voltage monitoring, and labeled GPIO.

caseStudy.statement: More flash and flexible power input in a Pico-sized board.
caseStudy.problem: Standard development boards can limit available storage and power-input options.
caseStudy.built: The RP2040 board combines 16 MB QSPI flash, USB-C, diode-ORed battery input, a 500 mA regulator, and VSYS sensing on ADC3. It also includes BOOTSEL and reset buttons, power and GPIO25 LEDs, and labeled headers.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes KiCad and manufacturing files, a BOM, CAD, and board photographs. The supplied third-party CircuitPython firmware is explicitly marked untested.

images.alt: Photograph of the Pico+ Devboard front

caseStudy.statement: One charging station that also supplies backup power during an outage.
caseStudy.summary: A LiFePO₄ charging UPS specified for 180 Wh storage and 250 W continuous USB output, with four USB-C ports, four USB-A ports, and automatic power-source switchover.
caseStudy.problem: The project began with too few outlets at a shared household charging station and a need to keep devices charged through power outages.
caseStudy.built: MacroUPS combines a 24 V LiFePO₄ battery, a mains supply, USB charging modules, and custom ideal-diode boards. Four USB-C ports and four USB-A ports share the enclosure, with fuses, switches, cooling fans, and a battery indicator.
caseStudy.difficulty: The ideal-diode board addresses periodic voltage drops described in inexpensive alternative modules, which could otherwise cause unwanted switching between battery and mains.
caseStudy.contribution: System concept, electronics design, and integration of the backup-power hardware.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes a finished-build photograph, enclosure CAD, wiring diagrams, and fabrication files for the final ideal-diode board. Capacity, output power, and switchover figures are documented specifications.

projects.title: MacroUPS

projects.title: NFC Desk Lock
projects.description: An ESP32 drawer lock using a PN532 NFC reader, servo latch, and photoresistor to relock after the drawer closes.

caseStudy.statement: Unlock a drawer with an NFC card and relock it after closing.
caseStudy.problem: The project replaces a commercial desk lock with a configurable NFC-based mechanism.
caseStudy.built: A PN532 reader sends card data to an ESP32 over I²C. Authorized cards trigger a servo latch; a photoresistor detects the darker interior when the drawer closes, followed by a configurable relock delay of 10 seconds by default.
caseStudy.contribution: Electronics integration, custom NFC-card design, and component enclosures. The README credits the servo holder as an existing design.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository documents the wiring, component cases, full assembly, and NFC-card PCB.

images.alt: CAD assembly of the NFC desk lock

projects.title: Sound Direction Finder
projects.description: An ESP32 sound-localization project using four INMP441 microphones and time differences of arrival to estimate a source's direction in 3D.

caseStudy.statement: Estimate where a sound came from using the arrival times at four microphones.
caseStudy.built: Four INMP441 microphones mount at known positions in a CAD frame. The project uses time differences of arrival to estimate the source direction, with two optional continuous-rotation servos for pointing.
caseStudy.difficulty: The microphone positions must be known for the timing differences to describe a direction.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository supplies assembly instructions, a wiring diagram, component specifications, and downloadable CAD.

images.alt: CAD frame for the sound-direction finder

projects.title: Four-Port USB Hub
projects.description: A four-port USB 2.0 hub PCB built around the SL2.1A in EasyEDA, with matched differential pairs and fabrication files.

caseStudy.statement: A practical first PCB: one USB connection expanded into four ports.
caseStudy.built: The board provides four USB-A ports carrying data and power, a power indicator, and matched D+/D− differential pairs.
caseStudy.contribution: A first PCB-design project built while learning EasyEDA with a Hack Club tutorial.
caseStudy.outcome: Gerbers, pick-and-place data, and the bill of materials are included for fabrication and assembly.

projects.title: Autonomous systems built for competition
projects.description: Robot control, autonomous routines, and iterative tuning developed for VEX competition environments.

caseStudy.title: Competition Robotics
caseStudy.statement: Autonomous and driver-control software across two VEX competition seasons.
caseStudy.summary: VEX V5 competition code spanning High Stakes and Push Back, with C++, PROS, LemLib odometry, and an autonomous-routine selector.
caseStudy.problem: Competition software must support changing robot mechanisms and selectable match routines.
caseStudy.built: The repository covers the 2024–2025 High Stakes and 2025–2026 Push Back seasons. Push Back moved from the default VEX SDK to PROS, adopted LemLib for odometry, and added a selector for autonomous routines.
caseStudy.difficulty: The autonomous selector replaces separate programs for each routine, while the season folders retain code for different robot builds.
caseStudy.contribution: Lead programming and co-captaincy, with ownership of autonomous and driver-control development.
caseStudy.outcome: The README records Worlds qualification in both seasons, a 2024–2025 state finalist finish, and a 2025–2026 state championship and Think Award.

projects.title: Models and simulations that learn, see, and move
projects.description: Applied machine learning and custom simulation work focused on real-time behavior and visual systems.

caseStudy.statement: Compare several vision pipelines for spotting failed 3D prints early.
caseStudy.problem: Spaghetti, layer shifts, and detached prints can waste printing time and filament before anyone notices.
caseStudy.built: The repository includes Haar-cascade experiments, a TensorFlow/Keras binary classifier, and YOLO object-detection training and webcam inference. Its README describes a dataset of more than 400 manually labeled images from real print scenarios.
caseStudy.difficulty: The project compares lightweight recognition, whole-image classification, and bounding-box detection to explore speed and localization trade-offs.
caseStudy.contribution: Computer-vision pipeline and application of detection models to a concrete manufacturing problem.
caseStudy.outcome: Training scripts, datasets, sample detections, and a demo video are included. The README does not report quantitative accuracy or measured filament savings.

projects.title: 3D Print Failure Detection
projects.description: A 3D-print failure-detection project comparing Haar cascades, TensorFlow classifiers, and YOLO detectors using 400+ manually labeled images.

images.alt: Example output from the print-failure detection project

projects.title: AI Cars
projects.description: A Pygame driving simulation that evolves neural-network-controlled cars through selection, mutation, and crossover on custom checkpoint maps.

caseStudy.statement: Watch driving behavior evolve inside a configurable simulation.
caseStudy.built: Each car uses a neural network to make driving decisions. Evolution selects and varies networks across generations, while custom maps and checkpoints define the driving task.
caseStudy.difficulty: Population size, mutation rate, and fitness criteria can be changed to experiment with learning behavior.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository provides a real-time visualization and tools for creating custom maps.

projects.title: AI Fluid Simulation
projects.description: A Python fluid-prediction experiment with PyTorch models and an interactive comparison between learned and baseline simulations.

caseStudy.statement: Compare a learned fluid predictor with its baseline simulation.
caseStudy.built: The project separates training, generated-starting-state tests, visualization, and interactive comparison into dedicated scripts. A shared simulation class contains the AI and baseline models.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes model-testing and interactive comparison tools. The README does not publish a numerical accuracy or performance benchmark.

projects.title: Useful tools and experimental playgrounds
projects.description: Desktop utilities, workflow automation, graphics experiments, and small tools built to solve a specific problem.

projects.title: Keepalive
projects.description: A static web app that keeps the screen awake, with timed and unlimited sessions, activity totals, and a floating control window.

caseStudy.statement: Keep the screen awake for a timed session or for as long as needed.
caseStudy.built: The app supports countdown and unlimited modes, pause and resume, daily and weekly active-time totals, and an optional floating control window using Document Picture-in-Picture. Browsers without native Screen Wake Lock can use a NoSleep.js video fallback.
caseStudy.difficulty: Wake locks can be released when a document is hidden. The session lifecycle handles visibility changes and transfers controls to the floating document in supporting browsers.
caseStudy.outcome: A static site with dependency-free regression tests. Native floating-window placement and OS sleep prevention still require checks in a supporting browser; the page releases wake locks rather than shutting down the computer.

caseStudy.statement: A browser platform bringing games, apps, and web access into one site.
caseStudy.problem: Serving a game catalog and proxy requires a running backend rather than static hosting alone.
caseStudy.built: The project combines a web interface with a Node.js/Express server. Its dependency manifest includes Scramjet and Wisp proxy tooling, PostgreSQL with Sequelize, Redis, and Socket.IO.
caseStudy.difficulty: The README requires server-capable hosting and documents deployment through managed services or a VPS.
caseStudy.contribution: I co-founded the platform and contributed to its build as the product grew. The README credits Interstellar for some proxy code and navigation, and 3kh0 for some game sources.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository publishes deployment instructions and the platform's live site. It does not provide a verifiable audience-size metric.

projects.title: 55GMS
projects.description: A browser-based games, apps, and proxy platform I co-founded, backed by a Node.js server.

projects.title: Soft Body Physics Sandbox
projects.description: An interactive Python/Pygame point-mass and spring engine with cloth, bridge, and earthquake demos, mouse dragging, and wall collisions.

caseStudy.statement: Explore deformation and elasticity by dragging simulated soft bodies.
caseStudy.built: Point masses and springs form deformable 2D objects, with wall collisions and mouse interaction. Stiffness, damping, and gravity can be changed through configuration.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes cloth, bridge, and earthquake demonstrations, a debug mode, and a reset control.

projects.title: Roblox Account Manager
projects.description: A Windows PyQt5 app for managing Roblox accounts, with Selenium-based login, saved-account controls, settings, and multi-instance support.

caseStudy.statement: Manage multiple Roblox accounts from one desktop interface.
caseStudy.built: The PyQt5 interface organizes saved accounts and settings, while a Selenium launcher opens authenticated browser sessions. Separate tooling supports multiple Roblox instances, and the app includes an integrated setup FAQ.
caseStudy.difficulty: The application targets Windows; multi-instance behavior depends on the Roblox installation.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository provides the desktop interface, account launcher, settings panel, and multi-instance helper.

projects.title: OCR Screenshot
projects.description: A Windows screenshot-to-text utility using Tesseract OCR, a global hotkey, and the native snipping overlay to copy recognized text to the clipboard.

caseStudy.statement: Select a screen region and paste its text without retyping it.
caseStudy.built: A global hotkey opens the Windows snipping overlay, sends the selected image through Tesseract, and copies the recognized text to the clipboard. The tool also prevents duplicate instances and optionally cleans up saved screenshot files.
caseStudy.difficulty: The workflow depends on Windows 10/11, Tesseract language data, and the quality of the captured text.

projects.title: Eye Break
projects.description: A PyQt6 desktop break reminder with configurable intervals, sound and tray alerts, and a countdown that pauses while Windows is locked or asleep.

caseStudy.statement: A configurable reminder to take regular screen breaks.
caseStudy.built: EyeBreak v3 provides work and break intervals, sound selection and volume, tray notifications, and startup-display options. Personal settings are saved locally, and closing the control window can leave the app in the system tray.
caseStudy.difficulty: The countdown pauses while Windows is locked or asleep; the tray menu provides an explicit way to quit.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes default settings and notification audio, plus an immediate-reminder test mode.

projects.title: Procedural Terrain Generator
projects.description: An interactive Pygame terrain generator that combines Perlin-noise heat, wetness, and elevation maps into reproducible biomes.

caseStudy.statement: Generate and explore terrain shaped by climate and elevation.
caseStudy.built: Separate heat, wetness, and elevation maps determine deserts, grasslands, rainforests, mountains, snow, and water. User-provided seeds make generated worlds reproducible.
caseStudy.outcome: The viewer supports panning, zooming, and regenerating terrain; the repository includes example renders.

projects.title: ASCII Video
projects.description: A real-time webcam-to-ASCII renderer using OpenCV and Pygame, with preserved colors and configurable character sets and sizes.

caseStudy.statement: Turn live webcam frames into a moving display of colored characters.
caseStudy.built: The application captures webcam frames with OpenCV and renders their visual content as ASCII. Character sets, character size, and output colors are configurable.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes rendered examples and a live webcam workflow.

projects.title: Nighttime Alleyway
projects.description: A procedural GLSL alleyway rendered on ShaderToy with ray marching, dynamic lighting, soft shadows, and a starfield.

caseStudy.statement: Build a nighttime scene from shader code rather than authored scene assets.
caseStudy.built: The final alley shader generates the ground, walls, lamps, and textures procedurally, adding lighting, soft shadows, and a starfield. A separate baseplate shader preserves earlier experiments.
caseStudy.difficulty: Ray marching is performance-intensive; the README identifies march and shadow step counts as adjustable quality/performance controls.
caseStudy.outcome: The final scene and the earlier baseplate experiment are linked as runnable ShaderToy projects.

projects.title: World Border Expansion
projects.description: A configurable Minecraft plugin that expands world borders after entity deaths, with per-world rules, mob-specific chances, and valid respawn handling.

caseStudy.statement: Start in a small Minecraft world and expand it through gameplay.
caseStudy.built: Entity deaths can increase the world border, with separate chances and distances for passive, hostile, and boss mobs. Configuration also supports health-based bonuses and per-world expansion rules.
caseStudy.difficulty: The plugin adjusts warning distance as the border changes and handles player respawns within the permitted area.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository documents the configuration options and includes a gameplay example.

projects.title: Tools that make contest practice faster
projects.description: Utilities created around competitive-programming workflows and repeated problem-solving practice.

projects.title: USACO Boilerplate Generator
projects.description: A configurable Python tool that fetches USACO problem details and generates starter code for terminal or file-based input.

caseStudy.statement: Remove repeated setup when starting a USACO problem.
caseStudy.built: The tool fetches problem names, input-file details, and statements, then combines them with configurable boilerplate templates. It supports terminal and file-based input workflows and copying commands for use in VS Code.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes editable configuration and two starter-code templates.
